findings.text: follow-on (record completeness): the fragment's per-pass Jev rerank cost column does not sum to its own total. The eight cost cells read 0.08, 0.08, 0.08, 0.08, 0.07, 0.00, 0.00, 0.04 (reproduced from the run's own pass logs, identical to those the fragment tabulates), which sum to 0.43, while the total row and the cost prose state USD 0.51 against the cap — a 0.08 discrepancy. The manifest's artifacts field repeats the same inconsistency: 'USD 0.51 (passes: .08/.08/.08/.08/.07/.00/.00/.04)'. By contrast the companion fragment's four rows (0.07/0.09/0.08/0.07) sum exactly to its stated 0.31, so a rows-to-total sum is the established convention. Consequently the cross-run figure 'USD 0.82 both runs' (0.31 prior + 0.51 remainder) inherits the same 0.08; a correct sum would read 0.74. No pass was omitted from the table (exactly eight pass logs exist) and the only extra run named — the final confirmation pass — cost 0.00, so the 0.08 is not an unlisted pass. The done-when is unaffected (the spend stays far under both caps); what fails is the fragment's internal reconcilability.

follow-on (evidence record): the fragment and manifest both cite a source-level context-quality distribution — 'sources (via representative) high 1,910 / medium 339' — that no retained log supports. context-quality.log holds only context_quality.py's output, whose sources field reads cq '<none>' for all 2,249 enriched sources (the Graph property sg.context_quality is null); the figure is produced by the separate source_cq.py, whose output was never captured to a log.
